catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class switches the aggregate hat state PV. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 binds the io.gpio and io.digital resource kinds and requires a pin and a value per call, while iocs/hat.py drives every configured pin from one state PV. This command has no input, writes the fixed truthy value 1 to the state PV and returns the PV read-back, so the package uses an x-cap id with an inline output schema.
catalogue_requests.summary: Drive the hat pins HIGH through the state PV and confirm the state PV reads 1.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class turns off both aggregate output PVs and confirms both. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 is per pin, and cap.imaging.illumination.v1 binds light.source and needs a channel and an intensity rather than the raw integer and hex-string PV writes of this stop. The command has no input, writes the fixed values state=0 and color='000000', and confirms each by a fresh read, so the package uses an x-cap id with an inline output schema.
catalogue_requests.summary: Write state 0 and color 000000 and confirm both PVs read back.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; no device, IOC, Channel Access server or hardware was attached or tested.

Shape: the card's TagDriver over the Channel Access PVs of the two upstream PVGroups. iocs.hat:IOC exposes the integer state pvproperty (write_state maps a truthy value to GPIO.HIGH and a falsy value to GPIO.LOW); iocs.rgb:IOC exposes the string color pvproperty (write_color parses a hex colour and sets the PWM duty cycles). The card hints call these IOC attributes; in the upstream runtime they are caproto pvproperties served as EPICS PVs, so the driver bridges the two PVs rather than in-process attributes. native is iocs.rgb:IOC (one of the card entry symbols); the state point cites the sibling entry symbol iocs/hat.py:34. The deployment prefix is operator data: native.py requires state_prefix and color_prefix because the two IOCs are separate processes and the provided supervisor configuration gives the hat IOC a templated prefix (supervisor_config/hat.conf:2) while rgb uses the default (supervisor_config/rgb.conf:2).

Points: state (integer, read-write) and color (string, read-write). The color PV is a one-element string array upstream (pvproperty(value=['000000'])); the tag point carries the single string and native.py flattens a one-element list. The color field accepts six hexadecimal digits, the format the IOC docstring shows; the endpoint pattern is stricter than int(value[0], 16), which would accept other hex lengths. The state PV has no numeric range in the clone, so hat_state is Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json shows the operator narrowing it to 0..1. No G4 warnings were reported.

Stop: safety_bindings.estop writes state=0 and color='000000' and confirms both with fresh reads; the all_off command is the same input-free safe-state action. It turns the declared outputs off but does not call the IOC shutdown hooks, so it does not reconfigure the pins, stop the PWM objects or call GPIO.cleanup. It is a software stop, not an independent physical e-stop (R1; no hardware e-stop is claimed).

Fake: RecordingTagTransport with placeholder initial values state=0 and color='000000'; it is an analytic stand-in, not a recording. It models only write_state's truthiness normalisation and the PV read-back; it models no GPIO pin, PWM waveform, gamma correction, brightness or board failure.

Hardware: native.py is a caproto Channel Access client (Context plus pyepics_compat get_pv; fresh get(use_monitor=False); put(wait=True)); it was never imported or run. The TagDriver refuses the hardware backend until a human signs reviewed_by with scope hardware, and reviewed_by stays null in driver.lock.json. A reviewer must confirm the deployed prefixes and both IOCs, the installed caproto client, and a put whose reply is lost.

Residual: the hat_on command writes the fixed truthy integer 1 and confirms the state PV reads 1; the clone shows truthy -> GPIO.HIGH but not the numeric RPi.GPIO.HIGH constant, so a reviewer should confirm the deployed library's HIGH value is 1. A hat_state parameter write reports applied as the value sent while the PV read-back is the normalised HIGH/LOW level, so that write has no verify predicate.

Licence: the clone has no LICENSE file; the card and lock record NOASSERTION and the licence class is unknown. Publication is a human review decision. The two x-cap ids are documented in catalogue_requests because no catalogue class fits the aggregate PV actions.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the TagDriver against iocs/hat.py, iocs/rgb.py, the supervisor configs and hats.yml, the tag-bridge preflight (hat IOC only) and every fact. The author also served the rgb IOC's color PV and made the e-stop write and confirm both IOCs, although the helper encodes no arrays and color is declared as the one-element list ['000000'] whose put hook parses value[0] (rgb.py:45-51), the shipped playbook deploys only hat.py (hats.yml:10-16), the shipped supervisor configs give BOARD pin 11 to both IOCs, and a hat-only deployment could not even connect. The reviewer narrowed the package to the hat IOC (native iocs.hat:IOC; one state point; the e-stop and all_off write state 0 and confirm it; the rgb IOC NOT COVERED with these reasons) and changed driver.py, fake.py, native.py (one prefix option), test_driver.py, facts.md and fixtures/conformance.json, regenerating reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and strict collect pass, digest unchanged (sha256:6ce76b1feaa320556282094ed323a8a0f1a3b0aeabdd6e51fb07ffc3673e5b1c). Stale author text: the RESULT.json notes and the all_off catalogue request still describe the colour PV, and the lock's install notes still name state_prefix/color_prefix (native.py now takes prefix). Matches the readiness prediction (hat IOC, R1). The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: The stop proves only that the IOC executed the put of state 0 (write_state drives the configured pins LOW), not the pin levels, and it does not run GPIO.cleanup; what is wired to the pins is not stated (LEDs per the repository). With the caproto server in labs/caproto/caproto a one-element string PV is unwrapped before the put hook (_data.py preprocess_value), so rgb's value[0] would be the first hex digit; that is why the colour PV stays out. hats.yml templates supervisor_config/hat.py.conf, a file the clone does not have.
